title: TypeScript: which security bugs does the compiler not catch?
short: Parse every input with a runtime schema, make `any` a lint error and check authorization in each handler, not in middleware.
answer: Before your next release, parse every untrusted input with a runtime schema, make typescript-eslint's type-aware `no-unsafe-*` rules errors and move authorization out of middleware into each handler. Judge everything else by whether outside data can reach a shell, a file path, a URL, an object merge, `eval` or raw HTML unchecked.
audience: Developers and tech leads writing production TypeScript for Node.js servers and React front ends, and the security people who review it

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Parse every input at runtime.
items.text: The compiler erases types and `as` casts[^tseveryday], and `JSON.parse()` and `.json()` return `any`[^tseany]. Parse bodies, params, headers and messages with a schema such as Zod's `z.strictObject()`, which rejects unknown keys[^zod].

items.title: Make the compiler and linter refuse `any`.
items.text: Keep `strict`, the default since TypeScript 6.0[^ts6], add `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`[^tsconfig] and lint with typescript-eslint's `strictTypeChecked`[^tsestrict]. Run `tsc --noEmit` in CI, because Node.js runs `.ts` files unchecked[^nodets].

items.title: Authorize where the data is read.
items.text: CVE-2025-29927 let attackers bypass authorization in Next.js middleware[^nextmw], and five more bypasses followed in 2026[^nextadv]. Check the user's right to each record in every handler and Server Action[^nextsec].

items.title: Keep input away from shells, `eval` and raw HTML.
items.text: Cross-site scripting, OS command injection and code injection rank 1st, 9th and 10th in the 2025 CWE Top 25[^cwe]. Use `execFile` with an argument array, never `eval` input, and render user text as JSX children.

items.title: Patch the framework within days.
items.text: React2Shell, an unauthenticated remote code execution bug in React Server Components rated CVSS 10, was disclosed on 3 December 2025[^react2shell]; CISA listed it as exploited, with known ransomware use, two days later[^kev]. Patch within the patching sheet's deadlines and run Node.js 22, 24 or 26[^noderel].

items.title: Where does outside data enter?
items.text: Find the handlers, Server Actions, webhooks and queue consumers the change touches, including Next.js folders in brackets[^nextsec], and check that each parses its input first.

items.title: Did it add `any`, `as`, `!` or `@ts-expect-error`?
items.text: Ask why for each one near outside data, then follow that data to the sinks in the traps above.

items.title: Who may do this, to which record?
items.text: Missing authorization ranks 4th in the CWE Top 25[^cwe]. Check ownership of the record, not just the login; a page-level check doesn't cover that page's Server Actions[^nextsec].

items.title: What leaves the server?
items.text: Return only the fields the client needs, and keep secrets out of `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variables, which reach the browser[^nextsec]. Send new dependencies through the supply-chain sheet's checks.

blocks.title: TypeScript traps and what to use instead
items: **`JSON.parse(body) as Order`.** The cast checks nothing, so a missing field or a wrong type flows on[^tseveryday]. Use `Order.parse(JSON.parse(body))` and treat `as` on outside data as a bug.

**`exec("convert " + file)`.** `exec` runs a shell, and Node.js says never to pass it unsanitized input[^nodechild]. Use `execFile("convert", [file])`, or `spawn` without `shell: true`. A command injection in the React Native CLI has been on CISA's exploited list since February[^kev].

**`merge(target, req.body)` and `obj[key] = value`.** A `__proto__` or `constructor` key in input changes every object in the process. oRPC's deserializer polluted the prototype before Zod validation ran (CVE-2026-28794, critical)[^orpc]. Use a `Map` or `Object.create(null)` and refuse those keys in merges[^owasppp].

**`path.join(root, req.query.name)`.** Path traversal ranks 6th in the CWE Top 25[^cwe]. Resolve the path with `path.resolve` or `fs.realpath` and reject it unless it still starts with the root folder.

**`fetch(req.body.webhookUrl)`.** Attackers aim it at internal services or the cloud metadata address `169.254.169.254`. Allowlist hosts, validate the IP address you connect to and disable redirects[^owaspssrf] with `redirect: "error"`. Before October's fix, Node.js validated `0127.0.0.1` as a different address than the OS used[^nodeoct].

**`new RegExp(input)` and nested quantifiers like `(a+)*`.** One crafted string can take exponential time and block the event loop[^nodeloop]. Cap the input length and use the `re2` package for patterns users supply[^nodeloop].

**`eval`, `new Function` and `node:vm`.** `vm` is not a security mechanism[^nodevm]. An expression evaluation flaw in n8n gave remote code execution and is on CISA's exploited list[^kev]. Run user code only in a separate container, and start Node.js with `--disallow-code-generation-from-strings`[^nodecli].

**`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` and user-supplied URLs.** React allows raw HTML only for trusted, sanitized data[^reactdom]. Allow only `https:` URLs, parsed with `new URL()`, in `href` and `window.location`, and enforce Trusted Types with `require-trusted-types-for 'script'`[^mdntt].

blocks.title: Tools that catch it
items: **tsc.** `strict` plus `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, which isn't part of `strict`[^tsconfig].

**typescript-eslint.** `strictTypeChecked` with `parserOptions.projectService: true` enables the `no-unsafe-*` rules, `no-implied-eval` and `no-non-null-assertion`. Add `no-unsafe-type-assertion` yourself[^tsestrict].
**eslint-plugin-regexp.** `regexp/no-super-linear-backtracking` flags patterns that can backtrack[^regexp].
**CodeQL.** `js/command-line-injection`, `js/path-injection`, `js/request-forgery`, `js/prototype-polluting-assignment` and `js/polynomial-redos` cover TypeScript too[^cql].
**Node.js flags.** `--disable-proto=delete` removes `__proto__`[^nodecli] but not `constructor.prototype`[^owasppp]. `--permission` with `--allow-fs-read` limits what your code reads[^nodeperm].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **React Server Components had a second critical bug.** An unauthenticated remote code execution flaw came in October, fixed in 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9 and 19.3.1[^rscoct].

**Next.js had ten serious advisories.** Five middleware or proxy bypasses in May and July, five critical remote code execution bugs from August to October[^nextadv]. Run at least 16.4.1 or 15.5.28[^nextsvg].
**`strict` is on by default.** TypeScript 6.0 turned it on[^ts6]. TypeScript 7.0, the native compiler, has no API yet, so typescript-eslint needs TypeScript 6 alongside[^ts7].
**Node.js 20 is end of life.** Node.js 26 has been Active LTS since 28 October; 22 ends on 30 April 2027[^noderel]. Type stripping, now stable, runs `.ts` files without checking types[^nodets].
**Trusted Types work in every major browser.** They became Baseline in February[^mdntt], and React passes `TrustedHTML` to the DOM unchanged[^reactdom].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Hand-written type guards for request bodies.** They drift from the types they guard. Derive types from the schema with `z.infer`.
**eslint-plugin-security as your main check.** Its README warns of many false positives[^eslintsec]. Triage typed lint and CodeQL findings first.
**Freezing built-in prototypes.** `--frozen-intrinsics` is experimental[^nodecli] and freezing can break libraries[^owasppp]. Fix the merges instead.
**Escaping shell arguments yourself.** Quoting rules differ between shells and Windows `cmd`. Drop the shell.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Treating the Permission Model as a sandbox.** It is a seat belt for trusted code, not a defense against malicious code[^nodeperm], and October's release closed two more gaps in it[^nodeoct]. Run untrusted code in its own container without secrets.
**Assuming a Server Action is private.** Anyone can call it with a direct POST, even if no page uses it[^nextsec]. Validate its arguments and authorize inside it.

blocks.title: What this looks like for your code

columns.title: New project
items: Start on Node.js 26 with `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `strictTypeChecked` as errors.
Write one schema per input and derive the types from it.
In Next.js, keep data access and secrets in a `server-only` layer that authorizes[^nextsec].

columns.title: Existing codebase
items: Turn on the `no-unsafe-*` rules as warnings and fix request handlers first.
Search for `exec(`, `shell: true`, `eval(`, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` and `as any`.
Move authorization from middleware into handlers, and leave Node.js 20.

columns.title: High-assurance or regulated
items: Make CodeQL's `security-extended` suite a required check.
Run services with `--permission`, `--disable-proto=delete` and minimal `--allow-*` grants.
Pen-test `proxy.ts` and route handlers regularly, as Next.js advises[^nextsec].
